Tetration

In mathematics, tetration (or hyper-4) is an operation based on iterated, or repeated, exponentiation. There is no universal notation for tetration, though Knuth's up arrow notation ↑↑ {\displaystyle \uparrow \uparrow } and the left-exponent

x b {\displaystyle {}^{x}b} are common.

Under the definition as repeated exponentiation, n a {\displaystyle {^{n}a}} means a ⋅ ⋅ a a {\displaystyle {a^{\cdot ^{\cdot ^{a^{a}}}}}} , where n copies of a are iterated via exponentiation, right-to-left, i.e. the application of exponentiation n − 1 {\displaystyle n-1} times. The number n is called the height of the function, while a is called the base, analogous to exponentiation. It would be read as "the nth tetration of a". For example, 2 tetrated to 4 (or the fourth tetration of 2) is ⁠ 4 2 = 2 ( 2 ( 2 2 ) ) = 2 ( 2 4 ) = 2 16 = 65536 {\displaystyle {^{4}2}=2^{(2^{(2^{2})})}=2^{(2^{4})}=2^{16}=65536} ⁠.
